messages.author: 40cb5026d0e9f97c
messages.subject: Fitting LGCP with covariates
parts:
I am trying to understand how INLA works for fitting LGCP models. 
I attempted to modify the very useful code in chapter 8 of the INLA SPDE manual to include a covariate (Eastings coordinate) as a deterministic term in the log-intensity.

INLA is crashing often and when it does not, the estimates of the intercept and the fixed effect are much less accurate than I would expect. 
I have not been able to relate this inaccuracy to some identifiability difficulty. 
So I guess I am doing something wrong. 


http://www2.imm.dtu.dk/~gigu/share/LGCP_INLA_GG.R

http://www2.imm.dtu.dk/~gigu/share/LGCP_INLA_GG.html

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Fitting LGCP with covariates
parts:
Hi,

the mesh you use is very sparse, which may be an issue.
You also most likely have edge effects creeping into your study domain
(due to the the Neumann boundary conditions and seemingly long spatial
range).
Try decreasing max.edge as well as increasing the domain extension.

However, inla crashing "often" indicates that something else is
wrong/problematic, but it's virtually impossible to tell what without
seeing the verbose diagnostic inla output (verbose=TRUE in the inla()
call).

Finn L

> So I guess I am doing something wrong.

On Friday, 28 March 2014 17:31:45 UTC+1, Finn Lindgren wrote:

Hi,

the mesh you use is very sparse, which may be an issue.
You also most likely have edge effects creeping into your study domain
(due to the the Neumann boundary conditions and seemingly long spatial
range).
Try decreasing max.edge as well as increasing the domain extension.

However, inla crashing "often" indicates that something else is
wrong/problematic, but it's virtually impossible to tell what without
seeing the verbose diagnostic inla output (verbose=TRUE in the inla()
call).

Finn L
